source.original_title: 05/19/2026 - Erenik Yzeiraj x Harry Edmonds KFS
source.display_title: 05/19/2026 - Erenik Yzeiraj x Harry Edmonds KFS — Follow Up

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: "is it the same number I had at a chat with your colleague, Kim?" and "Kim gave me a little bit of a head start anyway. He said you were more so focused on like health and longevity"

prospect.name: Erenik Yzeiraj
prospect.occupation: Private equity — desk job, part-owner of the business, currently leading his group's IPO process
prospect.family_status: Married, no children, actively trying to conceive; wife is athletic and does pilates and yoga
prospect.training_background: Highly active but never structurally strength-trained. Squash 2-3 hours a week over two sessions; soccer 5-6+ hours a week including club training Monday and Friday and a Sunday-league match; daily fasted core work at home for 10-15 minutes for the past three to four months. Repeated gym attempts that came "in small waves and small cycles". Kettlebell exposure limited to picking one up at the gym.
prospect.medical: Torn ligament in the right ankle with ongoing weakness — "my ankles have been weak, and I've had issues with the right one, I've torn a ligament there". Lower back soreness attributed to the desk job, which he reports has improved dramatically since starting core work. Knees reported as sound. Practises daily intermittent fasting, longest fast 20 hours.

signals: Already fit, athletic and training 8+ hours a week across two sports; buying incremental gain, not rescue — "Today, I'm quite fit and athletic, but no muscle mass"
Private equity partner leading an IPO; asked about payment structure and currency rather than affordability, and never questioned the number
Frames the purchase as a longevity and durability investment: "the more we age, the more we lose, the faster we lose muscle"

goals.text: Build muscle mass in a balanced way across the body
Improve mobility, particularly around hips and joints, testable through his soccer performance
Preserve muscle and function against age-related loss
Have a structure he actually sticks to for the long run rather than one or two months
Train at home without needing a gym or much equipment
Add upper-body strength on top of his core work without injuring himself

pains.text: Every previous gym attempt came in short waves; never had the motivation to stick to it
Never had a coach — entirely self-taught from online research, which he identifies as the number one impediment to his progress
Loses interest when there is no visible evolution — "If we do all the time the same thing, kind of get bored with it"
Dislikes crowded, performative gyms — "it's become too much of a show off with reels on Instagram"
Weak right ankle following a torn ligament
Lower back soreness from a desk job, improving with core work
Life events and a heavy, dynamic travel schedule have repeatedly disrupted training

objections.raw_quote: I'd have to think about it. Most likely it's going to be the 12, but I'd have to think about it.
objections.rep_response: Conceded immediately — "that's all good, man. That's all good. How long do you feel like you need?" — then changed subject to invoice framing for tax purposes. Later ran one useful clarifying probe: 'is it a decision of if I should do it, or is it which option to go for?'

objections.raw_quote: in full transparency, we're planning for an IPO of our group, so we're looking to hit the public markets at the end of this year, it's a very heavy process, I'm in the lead of it... just want to make sure that I can commit to it. I don't want to start and pause it.
objections.rep_response: Accepted it without any counter — "That makes sense. That's fine... Yeah, no, I appreciate it." Then moved to booking a follow-up. No OD play, no use of the pause/flex policy he had already described minutes earlier as the answer to exactly this problem.

objections.raw_quote: Do you, is there any flexibility on, on, on a monthly payment?
objections.rep_response: Quoted a monthly option at $1,200/month — "with the monthly payments you can, but it will be more money... it's like an extra 1200 at the end of it" — and steered to a 50/50 split within 90 days as the recommended structure. No isolate and no financial picture taken.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Three structures given: pay in full upfront (recommended, "put it on a credit card or whatever"); two payments of 50% — "3K down and then 3K, as long as it's within three months, within 90 days"; or monthly at $1,200/month, described as "an extra 1200 at the end of it", i.e. $7,200 total for the six-month programme.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: "we guarantee the results as well. So the only way we can guarantee a result for everybody is we do it on the weight of the kettlebell you're using... let's say you start off with a 16 kilo kettlebell. The guarantee is that by the end of the six months, whatever your starting weight is, you will be training with an eight kilo heavier kettlebell by the end of it... And if you're not at that point by the end of the six months and you've done everything we've told you to do, then we continue to work with you until you are there."

evidence: Explicit deferral: "I'd have to think about it" and "I should be able to confirm all to you and my continuation in the next 48 hours max"
Positive intent signals: "Look, I like it. The structure seems okay. And I think that June is going to be a good month to start" and a lean to the 12-month tier

Onboarding was pencilled for Monday 1 June, 7:15pm Switzerland time, but explicitly not booked — "gotta like onboard you first take payment and stuff like that... so I wouldn't be able to book it in now"
Counter-evidence: no payment, no payment link, and a genuine unresolved blocker — he is leading an IPO and stated "I don't want to start and pause it"
Next contact agreed over WhatsApp rather than a booked call — the rep offered Thursday 3pm Switzerland and the prospect declined the slot
outcome.next_step: Prospect to confirm within 48 hours via WhatsApp, deciding whether to proceed, which tier, and when to start around the IPO timetable; onboarding tentatively 1 June

notable.note: The best-qualified prospect in the batch — private equity partner, part-owner, actively training, no price resistance, explicitly good-to-great — and the call still deferred because the deep goals work and the consequence frame were never run. When he named the real blocker (the IPO), the rep had nothing to answer with, despite having described the pause-and-resume policy eight minutes earlier. Three items for a principal: the monthly plan is priced at $7,200 for six months; the guarantee was stated as 8 kg here versus 20 lb on the Robert Castillo call four days earlier; and the rep again volunteered to frame invoices "in whatever ways necessary for tax purposes". Also missed: the prospect explicitly parked a question about kettlebells for his wife and it was never revisited.

quality.notes: Frequent inversion, worst in the middle third. The rep's entire scheduling analysis at 00:07:00, his fasting explanation at 00:12:16-00:13:00, the guarantee statement at 00:24:22 and the travel-pause policy at 00:25:29 all sit under the prospect's label, while several of the prospect's replies sit under Harry Edmonds. Roles read from content throughout.
